8003.full: to burn round about: —; Pass. to be all scorched , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to slip away on all sides
8013.full: 1. with accusative to flow round , τὸν δ᾽ αἷμα περίρρεε (Odyssey by Homer); νῆσον π. ὁ Νεῖλος (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be surrounded by water , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to slip away on all sides , ἡ ἀσπὶς περιερρύη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν slipped off his arm into the sea, (Thucydides); [ αἱ πέδαι] αὐτόμαται π. (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to overflow on all sides , σοὶ περιρρείτω βίος may thy means of living abound , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὐδενὸς περιρρέοντος being superfluous , (Plutarch):—;Pass. to be all dripping , ἱδρῶτι with sweat, (Plutarch) (ML)

8014.full: περι-ρήγνυμι (Rec. -ρρ-, see supr.) [in LXX: 2Ma.4:38 * ;] to break or tear off all around: frequently of garments, τ. ἰμάτια, Act.16:22.† (AS)

8025.full: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

s: a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass
a going round in a circle, circuit
8028.full: 1. a going round, a flank march , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass , τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, τὴν π. in circumference , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. γῆς π. a chart or map of the earth (compare πίναξ); (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a going round in a circle, circuit , (Plutarch) 5. of Time, a cycle or period of time , (Pindar), etc. 6. a prescribed course of life, system , (Plato Philosophus) 7. a fit of intermittent fever, (Demosthenes Orator) 8. = περιφορά, a course at dinner , (Xenophon Historicus); π. λόγων table-talk , (Xenophon Historicus) 9. the orbit of a heavenly body , (Xenophon Historicus) 10. a well-rounded sentence, period , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

s: that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance
8029.full: περίσσευμα, -τος, τό (περισσεύω) [in LXX: Ecc.2:15 * ;] that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance: opposite to ὑστέρημα (which see), 2Co.8:13-14; pl., Mrk.8:8; metaphorically, π. τ. καρδίας, Mat.12:34, Luk.6:45 (cf. Ec, l.with; Plut., al.).† (AS)

8030.full: 1. very thoughtful, very careful, notable , of Penelope, (Homer) 2. like ὑπέρφρων, haughty, over-weening , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with genitive despising a thing, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

8050.full: 1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 2. metaphorically the complication of a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

8054.full: πλόος, πλούς genitive, -όου, -oῦ (and in late writers also πλοός, like νοός from νοῦς), ὁ (πλέω), [in LXX: Wis.14:1 * ;] a voyage: Act.21:7 27:9-10.† (AS)

8099.full: 1. springing forward , i. e. overhanging, abrupt , (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically = προπετής:—; comparative adverb, προαλέστερον more eagerly , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)
